root_cause.text: The RedBoot partition parser in `drivers/mtd/parsers/redboot.c` used `memcmp()` with fixed lengths against `names`, which can point to only the final `namelen` bytes of a dynamically allocated string, causing out-of-bounds reads when the name is shorter than the compared length.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `!memcmp(names, "RedBoot", 8)`, `!memcmp(names, "RedBoot config", 15)`, and `!memcmp(names, "FIS directory", 14)` with `!strcmp(...)`, and the CVE text says `"'names' is pointing to the final 'namelen' many bytes of the allocation ... This fortify warning looks legit to me -- this code used to be reading beyond the end of the allocation."`

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix RedBoot read-only partition detection to require exact name matches instead of prefix-based comparisons.
intent_record.what: The code inside the RedBoot partition parser changed three prefix-length `memcmp()` checks to exact string `strcmp()` checks for the names "RedBoot", "RedBoot config", and "FIS directory" before setting `parts[i].mask_flags = MTD_WRITEABLE` under `CONFIG_MTD_REDBOOT_PARTS_READONLY`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, only partitions whose names exactly match those three strings will now be marked read-only. Previously, the `memcmp()` calls compared fixed byte lengths and could treat any name with the same leading bytes as a match, so this change tightens the matching behavior and avoids unintended read-only marking of similarly prefixed names.

grouping_result.intent: Fix RedBoot read-only partition detection to require exact name matches instead of prefix-based comparisons.

relevance_review.reason: The change fixes RedBoot partition name comparison logic in the same parser and addresses the unsafe fixed-length matching against a possibly shorter dynamically allocated name, which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds read.

candidates.rationale: This fixed-length memcmp reads 8 bytes from names even though names may point to only the final namelen bytes of a dynamically allocated string, causing out-of-bounds reads when the partition name is shorter than the comparison length.
This comparison uses a fixed length of 15 bytes against names, which can be shorter than 15 bytes, leading to out-of-bounds reads in the vulnerable prefix-matching logic.
This fixed-size memcmp can overread names when the string stored there is shorter than 14 bytes, directly matching the root cause of unsafe length assumptions.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fixed-length memcmp compares 8 bytes against names even when names may reference only the final namelen bytes of an allocated string, so it can read past the available data.
This comparison uses a hardcoded length of 15 bytes against names, which may be shorter than 15 bytes, causing an out-of-bounds read.
This fixed-size memcmp can overread names when the underlying string is shorter than 14 bytes, matching the vulnerability root cause.
